trust_decision.summary: Whether a caller-supplied OAuth2 redirect_uri belongs to the client's registered redirectUrl is decided by a raw string prefix test in OAuth2Client.validateRedirectUri, called once in the /oauth2/authorize handler; the authorization code is not bound to the redirect_uri at token exchange.

landing_point.why: The only redirect_uri check in the repo; a grep for redirect_uri leads straight to the startsWith prefix test, called from the authorize handler at OAuth2AuthorizeController.java:69.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The token endpoint never issues a redirect, so an 'open redirect' fix seems complete once /authorize validates the URI; binding redirect_uri into the Redis code cache and re-checking it at /token looks like separate RFC 6749 hardening.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: In the default COMPATIBLE mode, sub-paths and extra query parameters under the registered callback must still be accepted (/callback/next, /callback?a=1&n=1), a registered bare origin must accept any path, and an omitted redirect_uri falls back to the registered URL at both /authorize and /token; exact-match-only or a mandatory redirect_uri breaks these.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An error-redirect branch (redirect to redirect_uri with error=access_denied/invalid_scope&state=...) that builds the URL from the raw param through buildRedirect.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: RFC 6749 4.1.2.1 requires errors to go back to the client's redirect_uri, and a maintainer adding it would reuse buildRedirect with param.get("redirect_uri") before or outside the validated branch.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A POST /oauth2/authorize (consent form submit) or response_type=token implicit-grant handler in the same controller that redirects to redirect_uri.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Consent pages and implicit grant are standard OAuth2 server features; a second handler copying the GET handler is a natural extension, and a solver could dismiss it as a different grant type.
